newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan VP to transit U.S. in Nicaragua trip.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan VP to transit U.S. in Nicaragua trip.

text.p: Taiwan Vice-President Lien Chan will transit Los Angeles when he makes a visit to Nicaragua in January, the state-run Central News Agency reported on Saturday.
Lien plans to attend the inauguration of Nicaraguan President-elect Arnoldo Aleman on January 10.

Lien's mission will leave Taipei on January 7, transit Los Angeles, and arrive in Nicaragua on January 9. He will depart Nicaragua on January 11, when he will transit the U.S. city again, before returning to Taipei, the agency said.
Lien said in December he may stop off in other countries to improve the island's diplomatic interests when he makes his trip to Nicaragua.

Nicaragua is one of only 30 countries -- mostly poor states in Africa and central America -- that recognise Taiwan's exiled Republic of China government instead of the rival communist Chinese government in Beijing.
Taiwan and China split after a civil war in 1949.
Beijing considers Taiwan as a renegade province and seeks to isolate the island completely from the international arena until it can be reunified with the mainland.

Taiwan newspapers had reported that Lien decided to visit Nicaragua out of fear that Taipei's allies may be tempted to ditch Taipei for Beijing after South Africa announced in November it would switch allegiance in 1997.
Pretoria had been Taiwan's biggest ally.
